Caramelised Root Vegetables

Served at: Autumn Equinox (Mabon)

Serves 4-6Prep 15 minCook 40 min

Caramelised Root Vegetables are a warm, earthy dish traditionally served during the Autumn Equinox, also known as Mabon. This dish celebrates the harvest season by highlighting the natural sweetness of seasonal root vegetables, making it a perfect accompaniment for festive meals honoring balance and gratitude.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups mixed root vegetables (carrots, parsnips, sweet potatoes, and beets), peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces (about 600 g)
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil (30 ml)
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter (28 g)
  • 2 tablespoons brown sugar (25 g)
  • 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves (or 1/2 teaspoon dried)
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar (15 ml)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
  2. In a large bowl, toss the root vegetables with olive oil, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
  3. Spread the vegetables in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
  4. Roast the vegetables for 25 minutes, stirring halfway through to ensure even cooking.
  5. In a small saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat, then stir in the brown sugar and thyme until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is bubbly.
  6. Remove the vegetables from the oven and drizzle the caramel mixture over them, tossing gently to coat.
  7. Return the vegetables to the oven and roast for an additional 10-15 minutes, until caramelized and tender.
  8. Remove from oven and drizzle with balsamic vinegar, tossing once more before serving.

Tips

  • Use a mix of root vegetables for varied texture and flavor.
  • If you prefer a vegan version, substitute butter with additional olive oil or a plant-based butter.
  • Add a sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley or rosemary before serving for extra aroma and color.
